solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old stuff frequently kept in emptied larders or other storage areas

parts.note: corn is trite, old-fashioned material, as in 'pure corn'

indicators.note: being kept in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other
an emptied word has lost all its insides, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: Antique goods are routinely stored in bare larders or in other places for keeping things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link: these storage areas are the alternative to larders. Corn as 'old stuff' means hackneyed material.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofts once used for keeping grain are storage spaces of a kind other than larders.

clue.text: Fish dish getting odd bits from chef as an enhancement

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish
a pie is a baked dish

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first and third, are picked out of the word chef

explanation.surface: A seafood meal gets random scraps from the cook to make it better.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cheeky: the Tudor pouch at the front of men's breeches was an anatomical enhancement.
explanation.definitionFit: This padded flap on hose served to advertise, and often exaggerate, what lay beneath, a showy augmentation.

clue.text: Just the opposite of near?

definitions.meaning: fair or correct, as in 'just and proper'
with horses and vehicles the near side is the left, so its opposite is the other side

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the near side of a horse or car is the left (the kerb side); the off side is the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Just means correct or fair, and the side opposite the near (left) side is the other one.

clue.text: Disillusioned writers flaunted intolerant egos

indicators.note: flaunted, loosely used for flouted, suggests the letters are paraded about and thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Bigoted, self-important authors showed off their attitudes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaunted' rearranges INTOLERANT EGOS.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was given to Hemingway, Fitzgerald and other American writers disenchanted after the First World War.

clue.text: Wild about edition covering several states

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: feral means wild, untamed

explanation.surface: A frenzied new issue of a publication goes out across many states.
explanation.definitionFit: A national government that spans a union of states, like the US one, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: New growth, small and nasty (friend's done for)

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: done for means finished off, so that piece is removed

parts.note: appalling means dreadful, nasty
a pal is a friend; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: Something fresh appears, minor and unpleasant, because a mate has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done for' removes PAL from APPALLING, leaving APLING.
explanation.definitionFit: A young tree is fresh growth in a wood or garden.

clue.text: Feel bad after encountering hard stones

indicators.note: after means this piece comes behind the other in the answer

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to ail is to feel ill

explanation.surface: Someone feels ill after running into hard stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Hailstones are the frozen pellets falling in a storm, so the stones of the weather are this.

clue.text: A course of action all but blocked by holy man with love for preacher

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective meaning belonging to or befitting an apostle, a preacher of the faith

indicators.note: something blocked by another has that other stuck in its middle
all but means everything except the final letter

parts.note: a policy is a planned course of action
ST is the abbreviation for saint
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A plan is nearly obstructed by a saint whose affection is for the man in the pulpit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' drops the last letter of POLICY; 'blocked by' puts STO inside A POLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to the apostles, Christ's first preachers, or to their mission.

clue.text: Assists cricket side to get trophies after opener's dismissed

parts.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field, the batter's legs side

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, and dismissed means it goes

parts.note: cups are trophies

explanation.surface: A cricket team is helped to win silverware after its opening batter is out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs; the opener is the first batter.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost or helping hand is an idiom for assistance, so these are things that assist.

clue.text: Laboriously teach and teach getting flak here?

definitions.text: Laboriously teach and teach getting flak here?

indicators.note: laboriously suggests the letters are worked over hard and so rearranged

explanation.surface: Teaching relentlessly while copping criticism is the daily lot of the classroom worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laboriously' rearranges TEACH, TEACH and FLAK; the whole clue describes the classroom front line.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means doing the real, hands-on work of teaching in a classroom, where the blackboard is.

clue.text: Artist put on show, timeless, revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the letters are read backwards
time is T, and -less means it is taken away

parts.note: staged means put on as a show

explanation.surface: A painter exhibited his work, ageless and radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' drops T from STAGED to leave SAGED; 'revolutionary' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was the French Impressionist painter famous for his ballet dancers.

clue.text: What swimmer may do with hot sexy costume could make you say "Oi"!

parts.note: a swimmer may take a dip
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a thong is a skimpy swimsuit

explanation.surface: A bather in a raunchy swimsuit could provoke an indignant 'Oi!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oi' is used for its sound: the vowel glides from O to I in one syllable, the very thing defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A gliding vowel sound blending two vowels in one syllable, as in 'oi', is the phonetic term.

clue.text: Number, say, resident in Bury

indicators.note: resident in means living inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to inter is to bury
e.g. means for example, which 'say' also means

explanation.surface: A figure, for example, lives in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the town but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number, with no fractional part, is the mathematical term.

clue.text: Egyptian chancellor's expression of current popularity provided by recording

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: 'I'm hot' is what someone in fashion right now might say
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A finance minister's boast that they're in vogue comes from a record.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient Egyptian was the pharaoh Djoser's chief official and architect of the step pyramid.

clue.text: The sort of order in which you'll find Matins, Vespers and Compline?

definitions.text: The sort of order in which you'll find Matins, Vespers and Compline?

parts.words: The sort of order in which you'll find Matins, Vespers and Compline?
parts.note: these church services fall at morning, evening and night, so the list is in time order; 'order' also suggests a religious order

explanation.walkthrough: Matins, Vespers and Compline are the morning, evening and bedtime offices of the church; 'order' teases with monastic orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Listing events by when they happen, earliest first, is time sequence, as these three services are.

clue.text: Theatre food coming round again

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
eating means food, as in 'good eating'

explanation.surface: Theatre snacks keep returning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recurring, happening once more, is coming round again.

clue.text: Bottom resident in apartment search?

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
to fish is to search, as in fishing for compliments

explanation.surface: A tenant on the ground floor is out looking for a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice, sole and their kin lie on the seabed, so they are dwellers of the bottom.

clue.text: Describing essential component in rôle taken by writhing lap dancer

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

indicators.note: writhing means twisting about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An exotic dancer squirming in her performance is key to the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writhing' rearranges LAP DANCER into ANDPARCEL; 'taken by' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something that is an integral, inseparable element of the whole.

clue.text: Under the weather, but over it as well?

definitions.text: Under the weather, but over it as well?

parts.words: Under the weather, but over it as well?
parts.note: feeling ill while flying above the clouds, high over the weather

explanation.walkthrough: 'Under the weather' means unwell; a plane passenger is literally above the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea caused by flying, while travelling high above the clouds, is this sickness.

clue.text: Thickest portion in meat dishes? On the contrary

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside another
on the contrary reverses the stated order, so the dishes go inside the portion rather than the other way

parts.note: a dot is a tiny portion
pies are meat dishes

explanation.surface: The fattest helping in some meat pies, or the other way about.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as written, a portion goes in the dishes; 'On the contrary' flips that, so the dishes go inside the portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopey means slow-witted, thick, so the superlative is the most stupid.

clue.text: Psalms and church feeding the old soul

parts.note: Ps is the abbreviation for the Book of Psalms

indicators.note: feeding means going into, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: ye is an old form of the, as in 'Ye Olde Tea Shoppe'

explanation.surface: Hymns and worship nourish the ancient spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word for the human spirit or mind is used in English for the soul.

clue.text: Shower? Shiver, getting cold not hot

indicators.note: getting introduces the letter that comes in as a replacement
not marks the letter that is replaced and goes out

parts.note: to shiver is to shatter into pieces
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: In the shower someone shudders, as the water turns cold instead of hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shiver' looks like trembling but is the old sense, to smash. 'Shower?' is a verb: to spray around.
explanation.definitionFit: To shower things is to strew or spray them all about.

clue.text: Somewhat fishy crumpet?

definitions.meaning: read as a little ... makes a small version, as in piglet
a small thick pancake eaten toasted, like a crumpet

explanation.walkthrough: A pikelet is a British and Australasian griddle cake much like a crumpet; the first reading invents a baby pike.
explanation.definitionFit: This small griddle cake, eaten toasted and buttered, is a regional name for a kind of crumpet.

clue.text: Plumber's brother, clumsy guy I found round Italy

indicators.note: found round means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a lug is a big clumsy fellow
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A tradesman's sibling, an awkward bloke, turns up touring Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The plumber is Mario of the Nintendo games.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nintendo hero Mario, a plumber, has a taller green-clad sibling who shares his trade.

clue.text: Hooped skirt, nearly half crimped, with no wrinkle

indicators.note: the word crimped has seven letters, so just under half of it is its first three

parts.note: a line is a wrinkle on the face

explanation.surface: A hooped skirt, partly crimped, has no creases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly half' keeps the first three of crimped's seven letters, just short of half.
explanation.definitionFit: This stiff Victorian petticoat frame, often of hoops, held skirts out wide.

clue.text: Gutted film industry backed by one's friends in Italy

indicators.note: backed means turned backwards
gutted means the middle is removed, here the two central letters

parts.note: cinema is the film industry as a whole
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: A movie business stripped bare is propped up by a person's pals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' removes NE from CINEMA to leave CIMA; 'backed' reverses it to AMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Italian plural word for friends, singular amico.

clue.text: Urge closure of eatery, following description of omelettes?

indicators.note: following means this last piece comes after the first

parts.note: to egg on is to urge

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone presses for a café to close after a critic's write-up of its omelettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Omelettes taste of and are made from what hens lay, so the adjective describes them.

clue.text: Playful friends accepting game half-heartedly

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: kith means friends, as in kith and kin

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its double letter in the middle, and half of that goes

parts.note: tennis is a game

explanation.surface: Fun-loving mates take on a sport with little enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two central Ns of TENNIS to give TENIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky and full of play, like a young cat, is what the adjective conveys.
